$comment: The state machines of docs/design/engine-protocol.md section 10 as data: the engine's runtime ordering checks and the conformance checker (maic protocol check, ctest protocol_conformance) both load this file. A machine has states, an initial and terminal states, and transitions {from, on (event types), when (JSON pointer into the event: allowed values), key (JSON pointers naming the instance; the machine's key by default), to}. An event concerns a machine when one of its transitions lists the event's type and its `when` holds and its key is present; it must then be legal from the instance's state. `openai: true` machines also run over the OpenAI-only view (rule openai.view); `scope: response` instances live inside the open response; `one_open` and `closes` are the response machine's rules response.one_open and response.items_done. The rules that are not a single machine (sequence numbers, turns, schemas) are listed with their ids and implemented in core/src/protocol.cpp. `filter` lists the event types a connection may be spared (`filterable`, named in maic.hello's `exclude`) and the types a capability covers (sent only to a connection that announces it); rule seq.filtered. The machine for reviews joins with step 10.

rules.text: The first event of a load has sequence_number 0 and is maic.session.state.
Each event's sequence_number, or else its maic.filtered_from or maic.merged_from (in that order) when it carries one, is one more than the last event's: a larger number is a gap.
A sequence_number smaller than or equal to the last one within a load is a protocol violation.

A connection is sent no event of a type its maic.hello answer lists in `exclude`. The first event sent after filtered ones carries maic.filtered_from, the first number filtered out; a connection that excludes nothing never gets it.
Every event carries stream_id, the id of the session whose stream it is on.
Every event fits event.schema.json: OpenAI's shape for OpenAI's types, MAIC's for maic.* types.
An OpenAI-shaped object carries no field beyond OpenAI's but `maic` (and `stream_id` on an event): MAIC's own fields go in one maic object.
Every request's params, result and notification fits maic.openrpc.json.
Every event is a legal transition of each state machine it belongs to; a terminal state takes no further event.
At most one response is open on a session at a time.
A response's terminal event comes after every item and content part it opened is done.
Items, content parts, their deltas and actions occur only inside an open response.
output_index is 0-based within the response, in `added` order, never reused.
A response that opens a turn carries maic.turn one more than the previous turn; a later response of the same turn carries the same number and names the previous response in previous_response_id.
A turn closes at the terminal event that carries maic.final: true; a new turn opens only after that.
maic.turn.paused comes only while a turn is open and none of its responses is: right after a maic.response.cancelled with maic.final: false.
response.steer.accepted, response.steer.failed and maic.steer.applied are legal only while a response of the turn is open or the turn is paused, and so before the events they cause.
Every request is answered exactly once, on the connection it came from.
With every maic.* event and every maic object removed, each event still fits OpenAI's ResponseStreamEvent and the response, item and content part machines still hold.

machines.name: session
machines.description: One per load of a session (maic.session.state). activity moves without changing the state.

machines.name: response
machines.description: One run of the agent loop. At most one is open per session.

machines.name: item
machines.description: One output item, addressed by output_index within its response: announced before its deltas, closed after them.

machines.name: part
machines.description: One content part of a message or reasoning item: added, its text deltas, the text's done, then the part's done.

machines.name: action
machines.description: A tool call, from its call item's done to its output item's done. A subagent's approvals carry `thread` and no call_id: they belong to the subagent's own stream.

machines.name: approval
machines.description: Requested, then answered once. A late answer is a request error (maic_already_answered), never an event.

machines.name: question
machines.description: Asked, then answered once (withdrawn: true when a steer took its place).

machines.name: steer
machines.description: One steer, by its id: accepted (response.steer, and maic.steer's steer, drop and further), applied (the six actions), or failed when a keep or halt ends the turn before its successor commits it. Its commit is the successor's response.created, which names no steer.
